title: Optimal transport mapping via input convex neural networks

nodes.text: A minimax optimization framework learns the optimal transport map between two distributions from samples by parametrizing the Kantorovich potentials as gradients of Input Convex Neural Networks (ICNNs), without any regularization.
nodes.evidence: we propose a new framework to estimate the optimal transport mapping as the gradient of a convex function that is trained via minimax optimization

nodes.text: This is the first instance where ICNNs are leveraged to learn optimal transport maps in a scalable fashion.
nodes.evidence: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first such instance where ICNNs are leveraged for the well-known task of learning optimal transport maps in a scalable fashion

nodes.text: Restricting the search to convex functions eliminates the intractable infinite constraints of the Kantorovich dual, replacing them via a convexification trick so the dual is solved without entropic or quadratic regularization.
nodes.evidence: we instead eliminate the constraints by restricting our search to the set of all convex functions ... solve the dual problem without introducing a regularization

nodes.text: The proposed minimax formulation is consistent: its solution yields the exact optimal transport map (the gradient of the optimal convex function), with established stability analysis.
nodes.evidence: We establish the consistency of our proposed minimax formulation in Theorem 3.3. In particular, we show that the solution to this optimization problems yields the exact optimal transport map

nodes.text: Unlike WGANs, which use optimal transport only as a distance measure and learn an arbitrary generator sensitive to initialization, this approach finds the actual optimal transport map and learns the same mapping regardless of initialization.
nodes.evidence: because WGANs use optimal transportation distance only as a measure of distance, the learned generator map ... is arbitrary and sensitive to the initialization ... our proposed approach aims to find the optimal transport map and learns the same mapping regardless of the initialization

nodes.text: Because the generator is the gradient of a neural network, it can naturally represent discontinuous mappings, allowing it to map a single connected support to disconnected supports with sharp boundaries, unlike standard continuous neural networks.
nodes.evidence: a gradient of a neural network can easily represent discontinuous mappings, unlike standard neural networks that are constrained to be continuous

nodes.text: The formulation builds on Knott-Smith and Brenier theorems: the optimal coupling is supported on the graph of the subdifferential of a convex function, and the gradient of its conjugate is the unique solution to the Monge problem under quadratic cost.
nodes.evidence: The crucial tools behind our formulation are the following celebrated results due to Knott-Smith and Brenier

nodes.text: The minimax objective replaces the intractable convex conjugate f* with a second convex function g, with the optimal inner minimizer g equal to f*; the constraint g in CVX(Q) can be relaxed to L1(Q) without changing the optimum, which empirically improves the algorithm.
nodes.evidence: the constraint g ∈ CVX(Q) can be relaxed to g ∈ L1(Q) without changing the optimal value and optimizing functions. We numerically observe that the optimization algorithm performs better under this relaxation

nodes.text: ICNNs are a representationally rich class for this task: any convex function over a compact domain can be approximated in sup norm by an ICNN, justifying their use as the approximating class.
nodes.evidence: any convex function over a compact domain can be approximated in sup norm by a ICNN to the desired accuracy

nodes.text: The approach is built on Taghvaei & Jalali (2019), bringing their ICNN-based Wasserstein-2 approximation idea into practice via a novel minimax optimization formulation.
nodes.evidence: This builds upon (Taghvaei & Jalali, 2019), where ICNN ... is originally proposed. We bring the idea proposed (Taghvaei & Jalali, 2019) into practice by introducing a novel minimax optimization formulation

nodes.text: Numerical experiments (e.g. Checkerboard and mixture-of-eight-Gaussians datasets) confirm the accuracy of the learned transport map versus baselines including Barycentric-OT, W1-LP, and W2-GAN.
nodes.evidence: Numerical experiments confirm the accuracy of the learned transport map ... The transport maps learned by various approaches on ‘Checker board’ and ‘mixture of eight Gaussians’ datasets
